column1: rung2
column8: 5 forms minted 2026-09-04 (seat09), refs cut from the real `fpc -Miso` oracle. Existing ladder__rung02_arithmetic already covers +/-/*/div/mod on positive operands (undeclared here, same baseline-left-alone reasoning as rungs 0-1). New: real_div = the `/` operator (real division, 6.7.2.2 "the value of x/y shall be the result of dividing x by y") -- FAILS both modes: SCRIP computes `7/2` as `3.00`, oracle says `3.50` -- `/` is being truncated as if integer division, not performed as real division. div_neg/mod_neg = the spec's own precise mathematical definition of div/mod with a NEGATIVE dividend (6.7.2.2: div truncates toward zero by the abs()-bounded identity; mod is defined so `0 <= i mod j < j` for j>0, regardless of i's sign) -- `-7 div 2` and `-7 mod 2` tested as SEPARATE witnesses (not one, despite being minted together) because they disagree: div_neg PASSES (`-3`, correct truncating division), mod_neg FAILS both modes (SCRIP gives `-1`, a C-style sign-follows-dividend mod; oracle/ISO require the non-negative `1`). unary = monadic +/- -- PASS both modes. mixed_type = integer+real mixed arithmetic (6.7.2.2 dyadic-operand table) -- PASS both modes. Two distinct real defects filed: FINDING-2026-09-04-seat09-pascal-rung2-real-division-truncates-like-integer-division.md and FINDING-2026-09-04-seat09-pascal-rung2-mod-wrong-sign-on-negative-dividend.md, both asked to hq_P. PARTIAL CURE since filing, observed by seat09 2026-09-04 re-running --only 2 while minting rung5: ladder__rung02_arithmetic_real_div now PASSES both modes (real-division-truncation is cured); ladder__rung02_arithmetic_mod_neg still FAILS both modes (the mod-sign defect is NOT yet cured, unaffected by whatever fixed real_div -- confirmed these are two distinct code paths, not one). STATUS stays RED on mod_neg's account alone. FINDING-2026-09-04-seat09-pascal-rung2-real-division-truncates-like-integer-division.md and the sibling mod-sign FINDING both left as historical record, not rewritten.

column1: rung3
column8: 4 forms minted 2026-09-04 (seat09), refs cut from the real `fpc -Miso` oracle. Existing ladder__rung03_if_while already covers if-then-else and a while loop whose body executes multiple times with a begin...end body (both left undeclared here, same baseline-left-alone reasoning as rungs 0-2). New: if_no_else = if-then with no else clause, both the taken (condition true) and not-taken (condition false, falls through with no output) paths in one witness -- PASS both modes. while_zero = a WHILE whose controlling condition is already false on entry, the classic naive-implementation trap where an off-by-one or do-while-shaped codegen executes the body once anyway (6.8.3.8: the body executes zero times if the expression is initially false) -- SCRIP genuinely tests the condition before the first iteration, PASS both modes, no defect. dangling_else = nested if with no enclosing begin...end, else attached to the syntactically nearest unmatched if per the ISO 7185 grammar (outer condition true, inner condition false -- resolving to the inner if's else prints 'inner-false'; a parser that wrongly grouped the else with the outer if would print nothing from that statement) -- PASS both modes, SCRIP's parser resolves it per the grammar. if_compound = begin...end compound statement as BOTH the then- and else-branch body of an if (the while's begin...end body was already covered by the baseline; this closes the same gap for if) -- PASS both modes. Unlike rungs 0-2, this rung minted CLEAN: all 4 new forms plus the pre-existing baseline PASS both modes, 0 new defects filed -- if/while control flow holds up; STATUS stays PASS.

column1: rung4
column8: 4 forms minted 2026-09-04 (seat09), refs cut from the real `fpc -Miso` oracle. Existing ladder__rung04_for_repeat already covers an ascending to-for-loop (single bare-statement body, 3 iterations) and a repeat...until with a 2-statement body (left undeclared here, same baseline-left-alone reasoning as rungs 0-3). New: for_downto = a DESCENDING downto-for-loop (6.8.3.9's own downto-equivalence: v := pred(v) each step, the mirror of the ascending to-equivalence's succ(v)) -- PASS both modes. for_zero = a to-for-loop whose initial value already exceeds its final value (`for i := 5 to 1 do`) -- 6.8.3.9's own equivalence (`if temp1 <= temp2 then ...`, no else) requires the body execute ZERO times; the classic naive-implementation trap (an off-by-one or do-while-shaped codegen executing the body once anyway) does NOT reproduce here -- PASS both modes. repeat_once = a repeat-loop whose until-condition is already true on the very first check (6.8.3.7: "statement-sequence shall be executed at least once") -- the deliberate CONTRAST case to for_zero, proving repeat's defining at-least-once guarantee -- PASS both modes. for_compound = a for-loop with a begin...end compound-statement body (closes the same compound-statement-as-loop-body gap rung3's if_compound closed for if) -- PASS both modes. Like rung3, this rung minted CLEAN: all 4 new forms plus the pre-existing baseline PASS both modes, 0 new defects filed -- for/repeat control flow holds up. STATUS stays PASS.

column8: 3 forms minted 2026-09-04 (seat09), refs cut from the real `fpc -Miso` oracle. Existing ladder__rung05_proc_func already covers one value-parameter each on a plain procedure and a plain function via heading+block (left undeclared here, same baseline-left-alone reasoning as prior rungs). New: no_params = a procedure AND a function each declared with NO formal-parameter-list at all (total omission, `foo;`/`foo: integer;` -- not empty parens, which ISO 7185 does not spell) -- PASS both modes. multi_param = one formal-parameter-list exercising BOTH grammar shapes at once, a comma-grouped identifier-list sharing one type plus a second semicolon-separated group of a different type (`combo(a, b: integer; c: real)`) -- PASS both modes. forward = the OTHER two procedure-declaration alternatives together (heading+directive, then identification+block restating only the name, never the parameter list again, per 6.6.1's own grammar) -- FAILS both modes: the forward-declared parameter `n` is unreadable (prints empty, not zero) in the block reached via the bare identification, though the identical parameter works correctly with no forward (heading+block together).
